subject: Post-call: prompt telemetry & PII storage — confirm scope and retention
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Ellen Park <ellen.park@pinebrook.io>
Cc: priyom.das@redwood.ai, secops@pinebrook.io
Date: Fri, 23 Apr 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: prompt telemetry & PII storage — next steps

Hi Ellen / Pinebrook SecOps,

Thanks again for the time today — really helpful to see the data flows in your ingestion pipeline. Quick recap and the items you asked us to confirm about how Redwood treats prompts and output telemetry by default (we'll surface a formal security summary in the follow-up pack):

Summary of what we discussed (short):
- Your ask: confirm whether prompt text or LLM output containing PII is persisted, where it lives, and how long it is retained. Also confirmation on log exports and the ability to purge.
- Scope: Hosted API evaluation (initial POC), potential Dedicated pool if we move forward.

Default behavior (hosted API) — initial answers:
- Request/response bodies: we retain request and response text by default for 30 days for operational debugging and quality analysis.
- Telemetry: aggregated latency and error metrics are retained long-term in anonymized form; per-request telemetry (trace ids, latency, error codes) retained for 90 days.
- KV caches and runtime ephemeral state: not persisted to long-term storage.
- Logs exported to customer-managed log sinks: only if customer has opted in / configured an export.
- Redaction hooks: we offer prompt-redaction on ingestion to strip or hash sensitive fields before storage.

Next steps I propose:
1) I'll attach a short matrix that maps "what is stored" to retention windows and controls (attached: redwood-prompt-data-matrix.pdf).
2) Priyom (cc'd) will send the technical clarifications on encryption, DPA/DSP terms, and exact field-level storage semantics.
3) If you'd like, we can schedule a short security deep-dive (30m) next week to walk your SecOps through the Dedicated option where retention is fully customer-configurable.

Let me know if the 30 day/90 day framing is okay as an initial answer — we'll also send a version that describes Dedicated and Private behavior (where you control the retention at provision time).

Thanks,
Aditya Rao

aditya.rao@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: prompt telemetry & PII storage — next steps

Aditya — thanks for the recap and the matrix. A few clarifying Qs from SecOps before we schedule the deep-dive:

1) When you say "retain request and response text" for 30 days, is that the full plaintext prompt and the LLM output? Or do you store a hashed/partial representation by default?
2) Who has access internally at Redwood to the stored request/response content (role-level)?
3) Is everything encrypted at rest and in transit? Are keys customer-managed for Dedicated/Private?
4) For the hosted evaluation, do you have an option to set retention to 0 days (no storage) or to redact specific fields at ingestion?
5) If we request a purge for a given dataset or user, what is the SLA for complete removal from all systems including backups?

Also attach our standard DPA request (I'll send separately via DocuSign) — please confirm who on your team will own that.

Quick note: Pinebrook is in the process of documenting data residency needs; we may require EU residency for production. Please include region-specific options in the next note.

Thanks — Ellen Park
Head of Security, Pinebrook Labs
ellen.park@pinebrook.io

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: prompt telemetry & PII storage — technical details

Hi Ellen — Priyom from Product (inference infra) here; tagging the short answers below and expanding on a few fields you called out.

Short answers (hosted API default):
- Full plaintext prompt and output: yes, by default we persist the request and the model output for 30 days. This is used for troubleshooting, quality monitoring, and evals.
- Hashing/partial storage: we provide ingest-time redaction hooks that can hash or strip fields before the request is written to long-term storage.
- Access control: role-based access; only engineers on-call and SREs with an approved runbook can access raw request/response payloads. Access is audited and requires justification.
- Encryption: TLS in transit; AES-256 at rest. For Dedicated/Private we support customer-managed keys via KMS (AWS/GCP/Azure) or HSM integration.
- Retention controls: Hosted default 30 days; you can request 0/30/90/365 via account config for Hosted (0 = minimal retention: only ephemeral telemetry kept for 7 days). Dedicated: retention policy is customer-controlled at provision time and can be set to 0 days. Private: totally customer managed.
- Purge SLA: For Hosted, we can initiate a targeted purge and confirm logical deletion within 48 hours; physical removal from backups may take up to 30 days (we provide attestations on request).
- Exports to external logging: We do not send request/response bodies to external sinks unless explicitly configured by the customer; telemetry-only exports are common (latency, errors, trace ids).
- Embeddings/cache: embedding caches are disabled by default; if enabled, they are retained according to the embedding cache policy and can be purged. KV cache is ephemeral at runtime and not persisted long-term.

Operational controls we can offer for the POC:
- Ingest-time field redaction (we can provide a small SDK wrapper or a Lambda pre-processor).
- Configurable retention windows per environment (eval vs prod).
- DPA & SOC2 artifacts: we can share DPA template and SOC2 Type II report.

I'll attach a short Ops note and a DPA draft to this thread for your legal/procurement team. If you want to lock in EU residency for production, we can provision a Dedicated pool in eu-west-1 and apply retention policies there.

Regards,
Priyom Das
Product Manager, Inference Platform
priyom.das@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: prompt telemetry & PII storage — confirm scope and retention

Ellen — thanks for the great questions. Quick confirmation and proposed next steps so we can move to a security call: 

Confirmations: 
- Hosted default: full request/response stored for 30 days (plaintext) unless ingest-time redaction is enabled.
- Dedicated/Private: retention and key management fully customer-controlled (can be set to 0 days).
- Encryption: TLS + AES-256; KMS/HSM available for Dedicated/Private.
- Access & audit: RBAC, just-in-time elevation for payload access, and audit logs retained per account (90 days default for access logs).
- Purge SLA: logical purge confirmation within 48 hours; physical removal from backups up to 30 days.

Attachments we shared in this thread: DPA_Pinebrook_v1.pdf (for legal review), redwood-prompt-data-matrix.pdf (what is stored vs retention), redwood-data-sovereignty-ops-note.txt (ops-level details and EU provisioning notes).

Next steps:
1) I'll send a calendar invite for a 30m SecOps deep-dive next Wed (Apr 28) — proposed 10:00am PT. Please confirm or propose an alternate.
2) If you can share your DPA via DocuSign, we will have Legal review and return with redlines within 48 business hours.
3) Priyom will lead the technical deep-dive and bring the SOC2 report and KMS/HSM integration docs.

Happy to jump on a quick call now if that helps.

Best,
